introduction: Ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, while proportion equates two ratios. SSC CGL tests compound ratios, combining multiple ratios, mean/third/fourth proportional, direct-inverse variation, and applied problems on income-expenditure, ages, mixtures, and coins.

concepts.explanation: To combine a:b, b:c, c:d into a:b:c:d, make the common terms equal by cross-multiplication (LCM method) across all ratios.
X/5=Y/7=Z/9 directly gives X:Y:Z=5:7:9. For reciprocal ratios like 1/M:1/N:1/O=3:4:5, invert to get M:N:O=1/3:1/4:1/5.
Compound ratio of a:b and c:d = (axc):(bxd).
Mean proportional of a,b = sqrt(ab). Third proportional of a,b = b²/a. Fourth proportional of a,b,c = (bxc)/a.
P directly proportional to Q: P=kQ. P inversely proportional to Q: P=k/Q. Extend to powers/roots as needed (P=kQ²/cube-root(R) etc.).
When a fixed quantity is added/removed from each term of a ratio changing it to a new ratio, use algebraic equation with common multiplier x.
Savings = Income - Expenditure. Use ratio tables for income and expenditure separately, aligning common terms via LCM to solve for savings.
Set up current values as multiples of a common ratio variable x, apply given conditions (age after years, coin value equations, mixture composition) to solve for x.

formulas: Direct proportion: P=kQ | Inverse proportion: P=k/Q
Combining a:b:c:d from a:b, b:c, c:d — equalize common terms via LCM

question_types.identification_method: Given a:b, b:c, (c:d) separately, asked to find combined a:b:c(:d).
question_types.when_to_use: Make common term (b, then c) equal across adjacent ratios by multiplying.
step_by_step: Write all given ratios in a row
Multiply terms to equalize the common linking variable between consecutive ratios
Multiply straight down each column to get combined ratio
question_types.shortcut: For reciprocal-form ratios (1/a:1/b), just invert given ratio to get a:b directly.
common_mistakes: Not equalizing common terms before combining

question_types.identification_method: Question explicitly asks for mean, third, or fourth proportional of given numbers.
question_types.when_to_use: Apply direct formulas: sqrt(ab), b²/a, bc/a respectively.
step_by_step: Identify type of proportional asked
Plug values into the respective formula
Simplify to get final answer
question_types.shortcut: Memorize the three formulas cold — these are single-step direct-formula questions.
common_mistakes: Confusing third proportional (b²/a) with fourth proportional (bc/a)

practice_questions.q: M=mean proportional of 16,9; N=third proportional of 9,15. Find 5M+3N.

question_types.identification_method: A fixed number is added/subtracted from each term of a ratio, changing it to a new given ratio.
question_types.when_to_use: Set original terms as ax,bx; form equation using new ratio after addition/subtraction; solve for x.
step_by_step: Represent original quantities using common variable x based on given ratio
Apply the addition/subtraction condition to form new ratio equation
Cross-multiply and solve for x
Substitute back to get required quantity
question_types.shortcut: For 3+ terms changing simultaneously by the same fixed amount, use LCM scaling to align before/after ratios directly.
common_mistakes: Applying the added/removed amount to wrong term
Not scaling ratios to common base before comparing

practice_questions.q: Boys:girls=5:6 initially. 40 boys leave, 50 girls join; ratio becomes 8:11. Find initial girls.
Marbles in 3 bags ratio 2:3:4; adding 12 to each changes ratio to 8:11:14. Find total initial marbles.

question_types.identification_method: Phrases like 'varies directly/inversely as', 'proportional to square/cube/root of'.
question_types.when_to_use: Set up P=kQ^n or P=k/Q^n, find k using given values, then solve for unknown.
step_by_step: Write the variation equation with constant k based on wording
Substitute known P,Q pair to find k
Substitute new Q to find required P (or vice versa)
question_types.shortcut: Watch for combined variation (P=k1x + k2/y) — treat as two separate constants and solve simultaneously.
common_mistakes: Mixing up direct and inverse relation direction
Forgetting the power/root in variation statement

practice_questions.q: M varies inversely as (N²+3). M=3 when N=3. Find M when N²=69.
Diamond cost ∝ (weight)². 14g diamond costs ₹2560, breaks in ratio 5:9. Find loss%.

question_types.identification_method: Income and expenditure ratios given (possibly with % increase), savings or difference asked.
question_types.when_to_use: Tabulate income and expenditure on common base using LCM; savings=income-expenditure; apply % changes directly on each row.
step_by_step: Write income ratio and expenditure ratio in separate rows
Scale rows to common base for the shared quantity (e.g., income)
Apply % increase/decrease to relevant row
Compute savings as difference and derive required %/value
question_types.shortcut: Align income and expenditure using LCM of their given figures before applying percentage changes.
common_mistakes: Applying % change to wrong row (income vs expenditure)
Not converting both ratios to a common base before subtracting

practice_questions.q: Income:expenditure=8:5. Income+20%, expenditure+30%. Find % change in savings.
A:B income=11:13, expenditure=9:11, both save ₹4000. Find income difference.

question_types.identification_method: Word problems on ages after/before years, coin denominations in a ratio, or mixture components in ratio.
question_types.when_to_use: Represent quantities as multiples of common variable x per the given ratio; apply the specific condition (years passed, total value, total legs/heads etc.) to solve for x.
step_by_step: Assign ratio terms as multiples of x
Translate word condition into an equation in x
Solve for x
Compute the specifically asked quantity using x
question_types.shortcut: For coin problems, total value = sum of (denomination x count) — set count as ratio multiples directly.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply coin count by face value for total amount
Errors in setting up age equations after years'

practice_questions.q: A:B ages=4:7. After 8 years ratio=2:3. Find sum of present ages.
Bag has ₹550 in 50p,25p,20p coins ratio 2:3:5. Find difference between 50p and 20p amounts.

identification_tricks: Two or more ratios sharing common terms — Combining Ratios type.
Fixed number added/removed from each ratio term — Ratio Change type.
Income and expenditure both given as ratios — Income-Expenditure type.
Real-world context (ages, coins, mixtures) with ratio given — Applied Ratio type.
solving_approach: Step 1: Identify what type of ratio relationship is being tested (combining, proportional, variation, applied).
Step 2: Convert all given ratios to a common base using LCM wherever multiple ratios interact.
Step 3: Represent unknowns as multiples of a single variable x based on the ratio.
Step 4: Translate word conditions into algebraic equations in x.
Step 5: Solve and back-substitute to get the specific quantity asked.
Step 6: Verify using the original ratio and given conditions.
shortcuts: Use 'by options' method for compound/complex proportional questions when direct algebra is slow.
For equal-value swap ratio mistakes (e.g. dividing wrongly), use difference-based shortcut: (sum of ratio terms) x (unit value from error).
Memorize compound ratio and proportional formulas cold for instant application.
For income-expenditure-savings, always place unknowns in a clear table before computing.
common_mistakes: Not equalizing common ratio terms before combining multiple ratios.
Confusing third proportional with fourth proportional formula.
Applying wrong direction (direct vs inverse) in variation problems.
Forgetting to scale ratios to a common base in income-expenditure problems.
Mixing up which ratio term corresponds to which entity in applied problems.
pyq_patterns: SSC CGL frequently combines 3+ ratios (a:b, b:c, c:d) into a single compound ratio.
Mean/third/fourth proportional formula-based one-liners appear almost every exam.
Ratio-change-on-addition (with a fixed number added to each term) is a recurring medium-difficulty pattern.
Income-expenditure-savings ratio problems combined with % increase are very common in Tier-1/2.
Age and coin-denomination ratio applied problems appear regularly as standalone questions.
quick_revision: Savings=Income-Expenditure (align via LCM before comparing ratios)
exam_tips: Always equalize the common linking term first when combining multiple ratios.
For variation problems, write the equation with constant k explicitly before substituting.
In applied problems, set up a clear ratio table (before/after) to avoid setup errors.
Use answer options to verify algebraic ratio answers quickly ('by options' method).

one_page_formula_sheet.income_expenditure: Savings = Income - Expenditure (common base via LCM)
